# flagset - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/flagset/0.4.7/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/flagset/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#welcome-to-flagset)Welcome to FlagSet!

FlagSet is a new, ergonomic approach to handling flags that combines the
best of existing crates like `bitflags` and `enumflags` without their
downsides.

[§](https://docs.rs#existing-implementations)Existing Implementations

The `bitflags` crate has long been part of the Rust ecosystem.
Unfortunately, it doesn’t feel like natural Rust. The `bitflags` crate
uses a weird struct format to define flags. Flags themselves are just
integers constants, so there is little type-safety involved. But it doesn’t
have any dependencies. It also allows you to define implied flags (otherwise
known as overlapping flags).

The `enumflags` crate tried to improve on `bitflags` by using enumerations
to define flags. This was a big improvement to the natural feel of the code.
Unfortunately, there are some design flaws. To generate the flags,
procedural macros were used. This implied two separate crates plus
additional dependencies. Further, `enumflags` specifies the size of the
flags using a `repr($size)` attribute. Unfortunately, this attribute
cannot resolve type aliases, such as `c_int`. This makes `enumflags` a
poor fit for FFI, which is the most important place for a flags library.
The `enumflags` crate also disallows overlapping flags and is not
maintained.

FlagSet improves on both of these by adopting the `enumflags` natural feel
and the `bitflags` mode of flag generation; as well as additional API usage
niceties. FlagSet has no dependencies and is extensively documented and
tested. It also tries very hard to prevent you from making mistakes by
avoiding external usage of the integer types. FlagSet is also a zero-cost
abstraction: all functions are inlineable and should reduce to the core
integer operations. FlagSet also does not depend on stdlib, so it can be
used in `no_std` libraries and applications.

[§](https://docs.rs#defining-flags)Defining Flags

Flags are defined using the `flags!` macro:

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
use std::os::raw::c_int;
flags! {
    enum FlagsA: u8 {
        Foo,
        Bar,
        Baz,
    }
    enum FlagsB: c_int {
        Foo,
        Bar,
        Baz,
    }
}
```
Notice that a flag definition looks just like a regular enumeration, with the addition of the field-size type. The field-size type is required and can be either a type or a type alias. Both examples are given above.

Also note that the field-size type specifies the size of the corresponding
`FlagSet` type, not size of the enumeration itself. To specify the size of
the enumeration, use the `repr($size)` attribute as specified below.

[§](https://docs.rs#flag-values)Flag Values

Flags often need values assigned to them. This can be done implicitly, where the value depends on the order of the flags:

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flags: u16 {
        Foo, // Implicit Value: 0b0001
        Bar, // Implicit Value: 0b0010
        Baz, // Implicit Value: 0b0100
    }
}
```
Alternatively, flag values can be defined explicitly, by specifying any
`const` expression:

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flags: u16 {
        Foo = 0x01,   // Explicit Value: 0b0001
        Bar = 2,      // Explicit Value: 0b0010
        Baz = 0b0100, // Explicit Value: 0b0100
    }
}
```
Flags can also overlap or “imply” other flags:

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flags: u16 {
        Foo = 0b0001,
        Bar = 0b0010,
        Baz = 0b0110, // Implies Bar
        All = (Flags::Foo | Flags::Bar | Flags::Baz).bits(),
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#specifying-attributes)Specifying Attributes

Attributes can be used on the enumeration itself or any of the values:

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    #[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]
    enum Flags: u8 {
        Foo,
        #[deprecated]
        Bar,
        Baz,
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#collections-of-flags)Collections of Flags

A collection of flags is a `FlagSet<T>`. If you are storing the flags in
memory, the raw `FlagSet<T>` type should be used. However, if you want to
receive flags as an input to a function, you should use
`impl Into<FlagSet<T>>`. This allows for very ergonomic APIs:

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flags: u8 {
        Foo,
        Bar,
        Baz,
    }
}
struct Container(FlagSet<Flags>);
impl Container {
    fn new(flags: impl Into<FlagSet<Flags>>) -> Container {
        Container(flags.into())
    }
}
assert_eq!(Container::new(Flags::Foo | Flags::Bar).0.bits(), 0b011);
assert_eq!(Container::new(Flags::Foo).0.bits(), 0b001);
assert_eq!(Container::new(None).0.bits(), 0b000);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#operations)Operations

Operations can be performed on a `FlagSet<F>` or on individual flags:

| Operator | Assignment Operator | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| | | |= | Union |
| & | &= | Intersection |
| ^ | ^= | Toggle specified flags |
| - | -= | Difference |
| % | %= | Symmetric difference |
| ! | Toggle all flags |

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-serde-support)Optional Serde support

[Serde](https://serde.rs/) support can be enabled with the ‘serde’ feature flag. You can then serialize and
deserialize `FlagSet<T>` to and from any of the [supported formats](https://serde.rs/#data-formats):

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flags: u8 {
        Foo,
        Bar,
    }
}
let flagset = Flags::Foo | Flags::Bar;
let json = serde_json::to_string(&flagset).unwrap();
let flagset: FlagSet<Flags> = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
assert_eq!(flagset.bits(), 0b011);
```
For serialization and deserialization of flags enum itself, you can use the [ serde_repr](https://crates.io/crates/serde_repr) crate
(or implement

`serde::ser::Serialize` and `serde:de::Deserialize` manually), combined with the
appropriate `repr` attribute:```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
use serde_repr::{Serialize_repr, Deserialize_repr};
flags! {
   #[repr(u8)]
   #[derive(Deserialize_repr, Serialize_repr)]
   enum Flags: u8 {
        Foo,
        Bar,
   }
}
let json = serde_json::to_string(&Flags::Foo).unwrap();
let flag: Flags = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
assert_eq!(flag, Flags::Foo);
```
## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [flags](https://docs.rs/macro.flags.html)
- Define flag value using the `enum`syntax. See below for details.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [FlagSet](https://docs.rs/struct.FlagSet.html)

- Error type returned when creating a new flagset from bits is invalid or undefined.

[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! flags using a `repr($size)` attribute. Unfortunately, this attribute
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! cannot resolve type aliases, such as `c_int`. This makes `enumflags` a
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! poor fit for FFI, which is the most important place for a flags library.
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! The `enumflags` crate also disallows overlapping flags and is not
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! maintained.
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//!
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! FlagSet improves on both of these by adopting the `enumflags` natural feel
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! and the `bitflags` mode of flag generation; as well as additional API usage
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! niceties. FlagSet has no dependencies and is extensively documented and
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! tested. It also tries very hard to prevent you from making mistakes by
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! avoiding external usage of the integer types. FlagSet is also a zero-cost
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! abstraction: all functions are inlineable and should reduce to the core
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! integer operations. FlagSet also does not depend on stdlib, so it can be
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! used in `no_std` libraries and applications.
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! ## Defining Flags
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! Flags are defined using the `flags!` macro:
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! ```
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//! use std::os::raw::c_int;
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! flags! {
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!     enum FlagsA: u8 {
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//!         Foo,
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!         Bar,
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//!         Baz,
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//!     }
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//!
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//!     enum FlagsB: c_int {
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//!         Foo,
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//!         Bar,
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//!         Baz,
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//!     }
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! }
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! ```
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//!
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! Notice that a flag definition looks just like a regular enumeration, with
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! the addition of the field-size type. The field-size type is required and
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! can be either a type or a type alias. Both examples are given above.
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//!
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! Also note that the field-size type specifies the size of the corresponding
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! `FlagSet` type, not size of the enumeration itself. To specify the size of
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! the enumeration, use the `repr($size)` attribute as specified below.
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//!
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//! ## Flag Values
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//!
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//! Flags often need values assigned to them. This can be done implicitly,
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! where the value depends on the order of the flags:
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//!
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//! ```
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//! use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//!
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! flags! {
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//!     enum Flags: u16 {
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//!         Foo, // Implicit Value: 0b0001
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//!         Bar, // Implicit Value: 0b0010
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//!         Baz, // Implicit Value: 0b0100
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//!     }
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//! }
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! ```
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//!
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! Alternatively, flag values can be defined explicitly, by specifying any
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//! `const` expression:
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//!
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//! ```
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//! use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//!
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//! flags! {
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//!     enum Flags: u16 {
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//!         Foo = 0x01,   // Explicit Value: 0b0001
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//!         Bar = 2,      // Explicit Value: 0b0010
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//!         Baz = 0b0100, // Explicit Value: 0b0100
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//!     }
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//! }
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//! ```
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//!
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//! Flags can also overlap or "imply" other flags:
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//!
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//! ```
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//! use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//!
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//! flags! {
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//!     enum Flags: u16 {
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//!         Foo = 0b0001,
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//!         Bar = 0b0010,
[126](https://docs.rs#126)//!         Baz = 0b0110, // Implies Bar
[127](https://docs.rs#127)//!         All = (Flags::Foo | Flags::Bar | Flags::Baz).bits(),
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//!     }
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//! }
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//! ```
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//!
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//! ## Specifying Attributes
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//!
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//! Attributes can be used on the enumeration itself or any of the values:
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//!
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//! ```
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//! use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//!
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//! flags! {
[140](https://docs.rs#140)//!     #[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]
[141](https://docs.rs#141)//!     enum Flags: u8 {
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//!         Foo,
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//!         #[deprecated]
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//!         Bar,
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//!         Baz,
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//!     }
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//! }
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//! ```
[149](https://docs.rs#149)//!
[150](https://docs.rs#150)//! ## Collections of Flags
[151](https://docs.rs#151)//!
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//! A collection of flags is a `FlagSet<T>`. If you are storing the flags in
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//! memory, the raw `FlagSet<T>` type should be used. However, if you want to
[154](https://docs.rs#154)//! receive flags as an input to a function, you should use
[155](https://docs.rs#155)//! `impl Into<FlagSet<T>>`. This allows for very ergonomic APIs:
[156](https://docs.rs#156)//!
[157](https://docs.rs#157)//! ```
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//! use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[159](https://docs.rs#159)//!
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//! flags! {
[161](https://docs.rs#161)//!     enum Flags: u8 {
[162](https://docs.rs#162)//!         Foo,
[163](https://docs.rs#163)//!         Bar,
[164](https://docs.rs#164)//!         Baz,
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//!     }
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//! }
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//!
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//! struct Container(FlagSet<Flags>);
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//!
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//! impl Container {
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//!     fn new(flags: impl Into<FlagSet<Flags>>) -> Container {
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//!         Container(flags.into())
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//!     }
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//! }
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//!
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//! assert_eq!(Container::new(Flags::Foo | Flags::Bar).0.bits(), 0b011);
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//! assert_eq!(Container::new(Flags::Foo).0.bits(), 0b001);
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//! assert_eq!(Container::new(None).0.bits(), 0b000);
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//! ```
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//!
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//! ## Operations
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//!
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//! Operations can be performed on a `FlagSet<F>` or on individual flags:
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//!
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//! | Operator | Assignment Operator | Meaning                |
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//! |----------|---------------------|------------------------|
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//! | \|       | \|=                 | Union                  |
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//! | &        | &=                  | Intersection           |
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//! | ^        | ^=                  | Toggle specified flags |
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//! | -        | -=                  | Difference             |
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//! | %        | %=                  | Symmetric difference   |
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//! | !        |                     | Toggle all flags       |
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//!
[194](https://docs.rs#194)#![cfg_attr(
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    feature = "serde",
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    doc = r#"
[197](https://docs.rs#197)
[198](https://docs.rs#198)## Optional Serde support
[199](https://docs.rs#199)
[200](https://docs.rs#200)[Serde] support can be enabled with the 'serde' feature flag. You can then serialize and
[201](https://docs.rs#201)deserialize `FlagSet<T>` to and from any of the [supported formats]:
[202](https://docs.rs#202)
[203](https://docs.rs#203) ```
[204](https://docs.rs#204) use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[205](https://docs.rs#205)
[206](https://docs.rs#206) flags! {
[207](https://docs.rs#207)     enum Flags: u8 {
[208](https://docs.rs#208)         Foo,
[209](https://docs.rs#209)         Bar,
[210](https://docs.rs#210)     }
[211](https://docs.rs#211) }
[212](https://docs.rs#212)
[213](https://docs.rs#213) let flagset = Flags::Foo | Flags::Bar;
[214](https://docs.rs#214) let json = serde_json::to_string(&flagset).unwrap();
[215](https://docs.rs#215) let flagset: FlagSet<Flags> = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
[216](https://docs.rs#216) assert_eq!(flagset.bits(), 0b011);
[217](https://docs.rs#217) ```
[218](https://docs.rs#218)
[219](https://docs.rs#219)For serialization and deserialization of flags enum itself, you can use the [`serde_repr`] crate
[220](https://docs.rs#220)(or implement `serde::ser::Serialize` and `serde:de::Deserialize` manually), combined with the
[221](https://docs.rs#221)appropriate `repr` attribute:
[222](https://docs.rs#222)
[223](https://docs.rs#223) ```
[224](https://docs.rs#224) use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[225](https://docs.rs#225) use serde_repr::{Serialize_repr, Deserialize_repr};
[226](https://docs.rs#226)
[227](https://docs.rs#227) flags! {
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    #[repr(u8)]
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    #[derive(Deserialize_repr, Serialize_repr)]
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    enum Flags: u8 {
[231](https://docs.rs#231)         Foo,
[232](https://docs.rs#232)         Bar,
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    }
[234](https://docs.rs#234) }
[235](https://docs.rs#235)
[236](https://docs.rs#236) let json = serde_json::to_string(&Flags::Foo).unwrap();
[237](https://docs.rs#237) let flag: Flags = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
[238](https://docs.rs#238) assert_eq!(flag, Flags::Foo);
[239](https://docs.rs#239) ```
[240](https://docs.rs#240)
[241](https://docs.rs#241)[Serde]: https://serde.rs/
[242](https://docs.rs#242)[supported formats]: https://serde.rs/#data-formats
[243](https://docs.rs#243)[`serde_repr`]: https://crates.io/crates/serde_repr
[244](https://docs.rs#244)"#
[245](https://docs.rs#245))]

[337](https://docs.rs#337)    #[inline]
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
[339](https://docs.rs#339)        while self.1 < F::LIST.len() {
[340](https://docs.rs#340)            let next = F::LIST[self.1];
[341](https://docs.rs#341)            self.1 += 1;

[343](https://docs.rs#343)            if self.0.contains(next) {
[344](https://docs.rs#344)                return Some(next);
[345](https://docs.rs#345)            }
[346](https://docs.rs#346)        }
[347](https://docs.rs#347)
[348](https://docs.rs#348)        None
[349](https://docs.rs#349)    }

[408](https://docs.rs#408)impl<F: Flags> From<Option<FlagSet<F>>> for FlagSet<F> {
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    /// Converts from `Option<FlagSet<F>>` to `FlagSet<F>`.
[410](https://docs.rs#410)    ///
[411](https://docs.rs#411)    /// Most notably, this allows for the use of `None` in many places to
[412](https://docs.rs#412)    /// substitute for manually creating an empty `FlagSet<F>`. See below.
[413](https://docs.rs#413)    ///
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    /// ```
[415](https://docs.rs#415)    /// use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[416](https://docs.rs#416)    ///
[417](https://docs.rs#417)    /// flags! {
[418](https://docs.rs#418)    ///     enum Flag: u8 {
[419](https://docs.rs#419)    ///         Foo = 0b001,
[420](https://docs.rs#420)    ///         Bar = 0b010,
[421](https://docs.rs#421)    ///         Baz = 0b100
[422](https://docs.rs#422)    ///     }
[423](https://docs.rs#423)    /// }
[424](https://docs.rs#424)    ///
[425](https://docs.rs#425)    /// fn convert(v: impl Into<FlagSet<Flag>>) -> u8 {
[426](https://docs.rs#426)    ///     v.into().bits()
[427](https://docs.rs#427)    /// }
[428](https://docs.rs#428)    ///
[429](https://docs.rs#429)    /// assert_eq!(convert(Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar), 0b011);
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    /// assert_eq!(convert(Flag::Foo), 0b001);
[431](https://docs.rs#431)    /// assert_eq!(convert(None), 0b000);

[721](https://docs.rs#721)impl<F: Flags, R: Into<FlagSet<F>>> Rem<R> for FlagSet<F> {
[722](https://docs.rs#722)    type Output = Self;
[723](https://docs.rs#723)
[724](https://docs.rs#724)    /// Calculates the symmetric difference between two sets.
[725](https://docs.rs#725)    ///
[726](https://docs.rs#726)    /// The symmetric difference between two sets is the set of all flags
[727](https://docs.rs#727)    /// that appear in one set or the other, but not both.
[728](https://docs.rs#728)    ///
[729](https://docs.rs#729)    /// ```
[730](https://docs.rs#730)    /// use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[731](https://docs.rs#731)    ///
[732](https://docs.rs#732)    /// flags! {
[733](https://docs.rs#733)    ///     pub enum Flag: u8 {
[734](https://docs.rs#734)    ///         Foo = 1,
[735](https://docs.rs#735)    ///         Bar = 2,
[736](https://docs.rs#736)    ///         Baz = 4
[737](https://docs.rs#737)    ///     }
[738](https://docs.rs#738)    /// }
[739](https://docs.rs#739)    ///
[740](https://docs.rs#740)    /// let set0 = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
[741](https://docs.rs#741)    /// let set1 = Flag::Baz | Flag::Bar;
[742](https://docs.rs#742)    /// assert_eq!(set0 % set1, Flag::Foo | Flag::Baz);
[743](https://docs.rs#743)    /// ```
[744](https://docs.rs#744)    #[inline]
[745](https://docs.rs#745)    fn rem(self, rhs: R) -> Self {
[746](https://docs.rs#746)        let rhs = rhs.into();
[747](https://docs.rs#747)        (self - rhs) | (rhs - self)
[748](https://docs.rs#748)    }
[749](https://docs.rs#749)}
[750](https://docs.rs#750)
[751](https://docs.rs#751)impl<F: Flags, R: Into<FlagSet<F>>> RemAssign<R> for FlagSet<F> {
[752](https://docs.rs#752)    /// Assigns the symmetric difference between two sets.
[753](https://docs.rs#753)    ///
[754](https://docs.rs#754)    /// The symmetric difference between two sets is the set of all flags
[755](https://docs.rs#755)    /// that appear in one set or the other, but not both.
[756](https://docs.rs#756)    ///
[757](https://docs.rs#757)    /// ```
[758](https://docs.rs#758)    /// use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[759](https://docs.rs#759)    ///
[760](https://docs.rs#760)    /// flags! {
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    ///     pub enum Flag: u8 {
[762](https://docs.rs#762)    ///         Foo = 1,
[763](https://docs.rs#763)    ///         Bar = 2,
[764](https://docs.rs#764)    ///         Baz = 4
[765](https://docs.rs#765)    ///     }
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    /// }
[767](https://docs.rs#767)    ///
[768](https://docs.rs#768)    /// let mut set0 = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
[769](https://docs.rs#769)    /// let set1 = Flag::Baz | Flag::Bar;
[770](https://docs.rs#770)    /// set0 %= set1;

[772](https://docs.rs#772)    /// ```
[773](https://docs.rs#773)    #[inline]
[774](https://docs.rs#774)    fn rem_assign(&mut self, rhs: R) {

[781](https://docs.rs#781)    ///
[782](https://docs.rs#782)    /// ```
[783](https://docs.rs#783)    /// use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[784](https://docs.rs#784)    ///

[791](https://docs.rs#791)    /// }

[797](https://docs.rs#797)    /// ```
[798](https://docs.rs#798)    fn extend<T>(&mut self, iter: T)

[801](https://docs.rs#801)    {

[808](https://docs.rs#808)impl<F: Flags> FlagSet<F> {
[809](https://docs.rs#809)    /// Creates a new set from bits; returning `Err(InvalidBits)` on invalid/unknown bits.
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    ///
[811](https://docs.rs#811)    /// ```
[812](https://docs.rs#812)    /// use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[813](https://docs.rs#813)    ///
[814](https://docs.rs#814)    /// flags! {
[815](https://docs.rs#815)    ///     pub enum Flag: u16 {
[816](https://docs.rs#816)    ///         Foo = 0b0001,
[817](https://docs.rs#817)    ///         Bar = 0b0010,
[818](https://docs.rs#818)    ///         Baz = 0b0100,
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    ///         Qux = 0b1010, // Implies Bar
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    ///     }
[821](https://docs.rs#821)    /// }
[822](https://docs.rs#822)    ///
[823](https://docs.rs#823)    /// assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b00101), Ok(Flag::Foo | Flag::Baz));
[824](https://docs.rs#824)    /// assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b01101), Err(flagset::InvalidBits)); // Invalid
[825](https://docs.rs#825)    /// assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b10101), Err(flagset::InvalidBits)); // Unknown
[826](https://docs.rs#826)    /// ```
[827](https://docs.rs#827)    #[inline]
[828](https://docs.rs#828)    pub fn new(bits: F::Type) -> core::result::Result<Self, InvalidBits> {
[829](https://docs.rs#829)        if Self::new_truncated(bits).0 == bits {
[830](https://docs.rs#830)            return Ok(FlagSet(bits));
[831](https://docs.rs#831)        }
[832](https://docs.rs#832)
[833](https://docs.rs#833)        Err(InvalidBits)
[834](https://docs.rs#834)    }

[836](https://docs.rs#836)    /// Creates a new set from bits; truncating invalid/unknown bits.
[837](https://docs.rs#837)    ///
[838](https://docs.rs#838)    /// ```
[839](https://docs.rs#839)    /// use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[840](https://docs.rs#840)    ///
[841](https://docs.rs#841)    /// flags! {
[842](https://docs.rs#842)    ///     pub enum Flag: u16 {
[843](https://docs.rs#843)    ///         Foo = 0b0001,
[844](https://docs.rs#844)    ///         Bar = 0b0010,
[845](https://docs.rs#845)    ///         Baz = 0b0100,
[846](https://docs.rs#846)    ///         Qux = 0b1010, // Implies Bar
[847](https://docs.rs#847)    ///     }
[848](https://docs.rs#848)    /// }
[849](https://docs.rs#849)    ///
[850](https://docs.rs#850)    /// let set = FlagSet::new_truncated(0b11101);  // Has invalid and unknown.
[851](https://docs.rs#851)    /// assert_eq!(set, Flag::Foo | Flag::Baz);
[852](https://docs.rs#852)    /// assert_eq!(set.bits(), 0b00101);            // Has neither.
[853](https://docs.rs#853)    /// ```
[854](https://docs.rs#854)    #[inline]
[855](https://docs.rs#855)    pub fn new_truncated(bits: F::Type) -> Self {
[856](https://docs.rs#856)        let mut set = Self::default();
[857](https://docs.rs#857)
[858](https://docs.rs#858)        for flag in FlagSet::<F>(bits) {
[859](https://docs.rs#859)            set |= flag;
[860](https://docs.rs#860)        }
[861](https://docs.rs#861)
[862](https://docs.rs#862)        set
[863](https://docs.rs#863)    }

[865](https://docs.rs#865)    /// Creates a new set from bits; use of invalid/unknown bits is undefined.

[890](https://docs.rs#890)        FlagSet(bits)

[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)/// Define flag value using the `enum` syntax. See below for details.
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)///
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)/// Each enumeration value **MUST** have a specified value.
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)///
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)/// The width of the bitfield **MUST** also be specified by its integer type.
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)///
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)/// It is important to note that the size of the flag enumeration itself is
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)/// unrelated to the size of the corresponding `FlagSet` instance.
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)///
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)/// It is also worth noting that this macro automatically implements a variety
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)/// of standard traits including:
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)///   * Copy
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)///   * Clone
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)///   * Debug
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)///   * PartialEq
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)///   * Eq
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)///   * From<$enum> for $integer
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)///   * Not
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)///   * BitAnd

# flags in flagset - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/flagset/latest/target-redirect/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/flagset/macro.flags.html

```
macro_rules! flags {
    () => { ... };
    ($(#[$m:meta])* $p:vis enum $n:ident: $t:ty { $($(#[$a:meta])* $k:ident),+ $(,)* } $($next:tt)*) => { ... };
    ($(#[$m:meta])* $p:vis enum $n:ident: $t:ty { $($(#[$a:meta])*$k:ident = $v:expr),* $(,)* } $($next:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Define flag value using the `enum` syntax. See below for details.

Each enumeration value **MUST** have a specified value.

The width of the bitfield **MUST** also be specified by its integer type.

It is important to note that the size of the flag enumeration itself is
unrelated to the size of the corresponding `FlagSet` instance.

It is also worth noting that this macro automatically implements a variety of standard traits including:

- Copy
- Clone
- Debug
- PartialEq
- Eq
- From<$enum> for $integer
- Not
- BitAnd
- BitOr
- BitXor
- Sub
- Rem

```
use std::mem::{align_of, size_of};
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum FlagEmpty: u32 {}
    enum Flag8: u8 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
    pub enum Flag16: u16 {
        Foo,
        Bar,
        #[deprecated]
        Baz,
    }
    #[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]
    enum Flag32: u32 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        #[deprecated]
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
    #[repr(u64)]
    enum Flag64: u64 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
    #[repr(u32)]
    enum Flag128: u128 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
assert_eq!(size_of::<Flag8>(), 1);
assert_eq!(size_of::<Flag16>(), 1);
assert_eq!(size_of::<Flag32>(), 1);
assert_eq!(size_of::<Flag64>(), 8);
assert_eq!(size_of::<Flag128>(), 4);
assert_eq!(align_of::<Flag8>(), 1);
assert_eq!(align_of::<Flag16>(), 1);
assert_eq!(align_of::<Flag32>(), 1);
assert_eq!(align_of::<Flag64>(), align_of::<u64>());
assert_eq!(align_of::<Flag128>(), align_of::<u32>());
assert_eq!(size_of::<FlagSet<Flag8>>(), size_of::<u8>());
assert_eq!(size_of::<FlagSet<Flag16>>(), size_of::<u16>());
assert_eq!(size_of::<FlagSet<Flag32>>(), size_of::<u32>());
assert_eq!(size_of::<FlagSet<Flag64>>(), size_of::<u64>());
assert_eq!(size_of::<FlagSet<Flag128>>(), size_of::<u128>());
assert_eq!(align_of::<FlagSet<Flag8>>(), align_of::<u8>());
assert_eq!(align_of::<FlagSet<Flag16>>(), align_of::<u16>());
assert_eq!(align_of::<FlagSet<Flag32>>(), align_of::<u32>());
assert_eq!(align_of::<FlagSet<Flag64>>(), align_of::<u64>());
assert_eq!(align_of::<FlagSet<Flag128>>(), align_of::<u128>());
```

use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    pub enum Flag: u16 {
        Foo = 0b0001,
        Bar = 0b0010,
        Baz = 0b0100,
        Qux = 0b1010, // Implies Bar
    }
}

assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b10101), Err(flagset::InvalidBits)); // Unknown

#### pub const unsafe fn [new_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.new_unchecked)(bits: F::Type) -> Self

Creates a new set from bits; use of invalid/unknown bits is undefined.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    pub enum Flag: u16 {
        Foo = 0b0001,
        Bar = 0b0010,
        Baz = 0b0100,
        Qux = 0b1010, // Implies Bar
    }
}
// Unknown and invalid bits are retained. Behavior is undefined.
const set: FlagSet<Flag> = unsafe { FlagSet::<Flag>::new_unchecked(0b11101) };
assert_eq!(set.bits(), 0b11101);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

This constructor doesn’t check that the bits are valid. If you pass undefined flags, undefined behavior may result.

Creates a new, empty FlagSet.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
let set = FlagSet::<Flag>::empty();
assert!(set.is_empty());
assert!(!set.is_full());
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Foo));
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Bar));
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Baz));
```
Creates a new FlagSet containing all possible flags.

        Baz = 4

Clears the current set and returns an iterator of all removed flags.

#### fn [bitand_assign](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/bit/trait.BitAndAssign.html#tymethod.bitand_assign)(&mut self, rhs: R)

Assigns the intersection of the current set and the specified flags.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u64 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
let mut set0 = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
let mut set1 = Flag::Baz | Flag::Bar;
set0 &= set1;
assert_eq!(set0, Flag::Bar);
set1 &= Flag::Baz;
assert_eq!(set0, Flag::Bar);
```
Calculates the union of the current set with the specified flags.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    #[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]
    pub enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
let set0 = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
let set1 = Flag::Baz | Flag::Bar;
assert_eq!(set0 | set1, FlagSet::full());
```

#### fn [bitor_assign](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/bit/trait.BitOrAssign.html#tymethod.bitor_assign)(&mut self, rhs: R)

Assigns the union of the current set with the specified flags.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u64 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
let mut set0 = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
let mut set1 = Flag::Bar | Flag::Baz;
set0 |= set1;
assert_eq!(set0, FlagSet::full());
set1 |= Flag::Baz;
assert_eq!(set1, Flag::Bar | Flag::Baz);
```
Calculates the current set with the specified flags toggled.

This is commonly known as toggling the presence

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u32 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
let set0 = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
let set1 = Flag::Baz | Flag::Bar;
assert_eq!(set0 ^ set1, Flag::Foo | Flag::Baz);
assert_eq!(set0 ^ Flag::Foo, Flag::Bar);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/flagset/lib.rs.html#666-668)[§](https://docs.rs#method.bitxor_assign)#### fn [bitxor_assign](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/bit/trait.BitXorAssign.html#tymethod.bitxor_assign)(&mut self, rhs: R)

#### fn [bitxor_assign](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/bit/trait.BitXorAssign.html#tymethod.bitxor_assign)(&mut self, rhs: R)

Assigns the current set with the specified flags toggled.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u16 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }

Creates a new, empty FlagSet.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
let set = FlagSet::<Flag>::default();
assert!(set.is_empty());
assert!(!set.is_full());
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Foo));
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Bar));
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Baz));
```
Add values by iterating over some collection.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    pub enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 1,
        Bar = 2,
        Baz = 4
    }
}
let flag_vec = vec![Flag::Bar, Flag::Baz];
let mut some_extended_flags = FlagSet::from(Flag::Foo);
some_extended_flags.extend(flag_vec);
assert_eq!(some_extended_flags, Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar | Flag::Baz);
```
Converts from `Option<FlagSet<F>>` to `FlagSet<F>`.

Most notably, this allows for the use of `None` in many places to
substitute for manually creating an empty `FlagSet<F>`. See below.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
fn convert(v: impl Into<FlagSet<Flag>>) -> u8 {
    v.into().bits()
}
assert_eq!(convert(Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar), 0b011);
assert_eq!(convert(Flag::Foo), 0b001);
assert_eq!(convert(None), 0b000);
```

### impl<F: Flags> [IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html) for [FlagSet](https://docs.rs/struct.FlagSet.html)<F>

Iterate over the flags in the set.

**NOTE**: The order in which the flags are iterated is undefined.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
let set = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
let mut iter = set.into_iter();
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(Flag::Foo));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(Flag::Bar));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), None);
```
Calculates the complement of the current set.

In common parlance, this returns the set of all possible flags that are not in the current set.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    #[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]
    enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 1 << 0,
        Bar = 1 << 1,
        Baz = 1 << 2
    }
}
let set = !FlagSet::from(Flag::Foo);
assert!(!set.is_empty());
assert!(!set.is_full());
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Foo));
assert!(set.contains(Flag::Bar));
assert!(set.contains(Flag::Baz));
```
Calculates the symmetric difference between two sets.

The symmetric difference between two sets is the set of all flags that appear in one set or the other, but not both.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    pub enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 1,
        Bar = 2,
        Baz = 4
    }
}
let set0 = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
let set1 = Flag::Baz | Flag::Bar;
assert_eq!(set0 % set1, Flag::Foo | Flag::Baz);
```

# InvalidBits in flagset - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/flagset/latest/target-redirect/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/flagset/struct.InvalidBits.html

`pub struct InvalidBits;`## Expand description

Error type returned when creating a new flagset from bits is invalid or undefined.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    pub enum Flag: u16 {
        Foo = 0b0001,
        Bar = 0b0010,
        Baz = 0b0100,
        Qux = 0b1010, // Implies Bar
    }
}
assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b01101), Err(flagset::InvalidBits)); // Invalid
assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b10101), Err(flagset::InvalidBits)); // Unknown
```

# flagset - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/flagset/latest/target-redirect/flagset/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#welcome-to-flagset)Welcome to FlagSet!

FlagSet is a new, ergonomic approach to handling flags that combines the
best of existing crates like `bitflags` and `enumflags` without their
downsides.

[§](https://docs.rs#existing-implementations)Existing Implementations

The `bitflags` crate has long been part of the Rust ecosystem.
Unfortunately, it doesn’t feel like natural Rust. The `bitflags` crate
uses a weird struct format to define flags. Flags themselves are just
integers constants, so there is little type-safety involved. But it doesn’t
have any dependencies. It also allows you to define implied flags (otherwise
known as overlapping flags).

The `enumflags` crate tried to improve on `bitflags` by using enumerations
to define flags. This was a big improvement to the natural feel of the code.
Unfortunately, there are some design flaws. To generate the flags,
procedural macros were used. This implied two separate crates plus
additional dependencies. Further, `enumflags` specifies the size of the
flags using a `repr($size)` attribute. Unfortunately, this attribute
cannot resolve type aliases, such as `c_int`. This makes `enumflags` a
poor fit for FFI, which is the most important place for a flags library.
The `enumflags` crate also disallows overlapping flags and is not
maintained.

FlagSet improves on both of these by adopting the `enumflags` natural feel
and the `bitflags` mode of flag generation; as well as additional API usage
niceties. FlagSet has no dependencies and is extensively documented and
tested. It also tries very hard to prevent you from making mistakes by
avoiding external usage of the integer types. FlagSet is also a zero-cost
abstraction: all functions are inlineable and should reduce to the core
integer operations. FlagSet also does not depend on stdlib, so it can be
used in `no_std` libraries and applications.

[§](https://docs.rs#defining-flags)Defining Flags

Flags are defined using the `flags!` macro:

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
use std::os::raw::c_int;
flags! {
    enum FlagsA: u8 {
        Foo,
        Bar,
        Baz,
    }
    enum FlagsB: c_int {
        Foo,
        Bar,
        Baz,
    }
}
```
Notice that a flag definition looks just like a regular enumeration, with the addition of the field-size type. The field-size type is required and can be either a type or a type alias. Both examples are given above.

Also note that the field-size type specifies the size of the corresponding
`FlagSet` type, not size of the enumeration itself. To specify the size of
the enumeration, use the `repr($size)` attribute as specified below.

[§](https://docs.rs#flag-values)Flag Values

Flags often need values assigned to them. This can be done implicitly, where the value depends on the order of the flags:

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flags: u16 {
        Foo, // Implicit Value: 0b0001
        Bar, // Implicit Value: 0b0010
        Baz, // Implicit Value: 0b0100
    }
}
```
Alternatively, flag values can be defined explicitly, by specifying any
`const` expression:

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flags: u16 {
        Foo = 0x01,   // Explicit Value: 0b0001
        Bar = 2,      // Explicit Value: 0b0010
        Baz = 0b0100, // Explicit Value: 0b0100
    }
}
```
Flags can also overlap or “imply” other flags:

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flags: u16 {
        Foo = 0b0001,
        Bar = 0b0010,
        Baz = 0b0110, // Implies Bar
        All = (Flags::Foo | Flags::Bar | Flags::Baz).bits(),
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#specifying-attributes)Specifying Attributes

Attributes can be used on the enumeration itself or any of the values:

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    #[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]
    enum Flags: u8 {
        Foo,
        #[deprecated]
        Bar,
        Baz,
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#collections-of-flags)Collections of Flags

A collection of flags is a `FlagSet<T>`. If you are storing the flags in
memory, the raw `FlagSet<T>` type should be used. However, if you want to
receive flags as an input to a function, you should use
`impl Into<FlagSet<T>>`. This allows for very ergonomic APIs:

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flags: u8 {
        Foo,
        Bar,
        Baz,
    }
}
struct Container(FlagSet<Flags>);
impl Container {
    fn new(flags: impl Into<FlagSet<Flags>>) -> Container {
        Container(flags.into())
    }
}
assert_eq!(Container::new(Flags::Foo | Flags::Bar).0.bits(), 0b011);
assert_eq!(Container::new(Flags::Foo).0.bits(), 0b001);
assert_eq!(Container::new(None).0.bits(), 0b000);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#operations)Operations

Operations can be performed on a `FlagSet<F>` or on individual flags:

| Operator | Assignment Operator | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| | | |= | Union |
| & | &= | Intersection |
| ^ | ^= | Toggle specified flags |
| - | -= | Difference |
| % | %= | Symmetric difference |
| ! | Toggle all flags |

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-serde-support)Optional Serde support

[Serde](https://serde.rs/) support can be enabled with the ‘serde’ feature flag. You can then serialize and
deserialize `FlagSet<T>` to and from any of the [supported formats](https://serde.rs/#data-formats):

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flags: u8 {
        Foo,
        Bar,
    }
}
let flagset = Flags::Foo | Flags::Bar;
let json = serde_json::to_string(&flagset).unwrap();
let flagset: FlagSet<Flags> = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
assert_eq!(flagset.bits(), 0b011);
```
For serialization and deserialization of flags enum itself, you can use the [ serde_repr](https://crates.io/crates/serde_repr) crate
(or implement

`serde::ser::Serialize` and `serde:de::Deserialize` manually), combined with the
appropriate `repr` attribute:```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
use serde_repr::{Serialize_repr, Deserialize_repr};
flags! {
   #[repr(u8)]
   #[derive(Deserialize_repr, Serialize_repr)]
   enum Flags: u8 {
        Foo,
        Bar,
   }
}
let json = serde_json::to_string(&Flags::Foo).unwrap();
let flag: Flags = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
assert_eq!(flag, Flags::Foo);
```
## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [flags](https://docs.rs/macro.flags.html)
- Define flag value using the `enum`syntax. See below for details.

[33](https://docs.rs#33)//!
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! The `enumflags` crate tried to improve on `bitflags` by using enumerations
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! to define flags. This was a big improvement to the natural feel of the code.
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! Unfortunately, there are some design flaws. To generate the flags,
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! procedural macros were used. This implied two separate crates plus
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! additional dependencies. Further, `enumflags` specifies the size of the
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! flags using a `repr($size)` attribute. Unfortunately, this attribute
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! cannot resolve type aliases, such as `c_int`. This makes `enumflags` a
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! poor fit for FFI, which is the most important place for a flags library.
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! The `enumflags` crate also disallows overlapping flags and is not
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! maintained.
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//!
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! FlagSet improves on both of these by adopting the `enumflags` natural feel
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! and the `bitflags` mode of flag generation; as well as additional API usage
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! niceties. FlagSet has no dependencies and is extensively documented and
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! tested. It also tries very hard to prevent you from making mistakes by
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! avoiding external usage of the integer types. FlagSet is also a zero-cost
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! abstraction: all functions are inlineable and should reduce to the core
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! integer operations. FlagSet also does not depend on stdlib, so it can be
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! used in `no_std` libraries and applications.
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! ## Defining Flags
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! Flags are defined using the `flags!` macro:
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! ```
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//! use std::os::raw::c_int;
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! flags! {
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!     enum FlagsA: u8 {
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//!         Foo,
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!         Bar,
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//!         Baz,
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//!     }
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//!
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//!     enum FlagsB: c_int {
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//!         Foo,
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//!         Bar,
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//!         Baz,
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//!     }
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! }
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! ```
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//!
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! Notice that a flag definition looks just like a regular enumeration, with
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! the addition of the field-size type. The field-size type is required and
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! can be either a type or a type alias. Both examples are given above.
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//!
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! Also note that the field-size type specifies the size of the corresponding
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! `FlagSet` type, not size of the enumeration itself. To specify the size of
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! the enumeration, use the `repr($size)` attribute as specified below.
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//!
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//! ## Flag Values
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//!
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//! Flags often need values assigned to them. This can be done implicitly,
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! where the value depends on the order of the flags:
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//!
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//! ```
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//! use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//!
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! flags! {
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//!     enum Flags: u16 {
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//!         Foo, // Implicit Value: 0b0001
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//!         Bar, // Implicit Value: 0b0010
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//!         Baz, // Implicit Value: 0b0100
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//!     }
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//! }
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! ```
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//!
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! Alternatively, flag values can be defined explicitly, by specifying any
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//! `const` expression:
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//!
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//! ```
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//! use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//!
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//! flags! {
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//!     enum Flags: u16 {
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//!         Foo = 0x01,   // Explicit Value: 0b0001
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//!         Bar = 2,      // Explicit Value: 0b0010
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//!         Baz = 0b0100, // Explicit Value: 0b0100
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//!     }
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//! }
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//! ```
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//!
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//! Flags can also overlap or "imply" other flags:
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//!
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//! ```
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//! use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//!
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//! flags! {
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//!     enum Flags: u16 {
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//!         Foo = 0b0001,
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//!         Bar = 0b0010,
[126](https://docs.rs#126)//!         Baz = 0b0110, // Implies Bar
[127](https://docs.rs#127)//!         All = (Flags::Foo | Flags::Bar | Flags::Baz).bits(),
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//!     }
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//! }
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//! ```
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//!
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//! ## Specifying Attributes
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//!
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//! Attributes can be used on the enumeration itself or any of the values:
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//!
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//! ```
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//! use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//!
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//! flags! {
[140](https://docs.rs#140)//!     #[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]
[141](https://docs.rs#141)//!     enum Flags: u8 {
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//!         Foo,
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//!         #[deprecated]
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//!         Bar,
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//!         Baz,
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//!     }
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//! }
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//! ```
[149](https://docs.rs#149)//!
[150](https://docs.rs#150)//! ## Collections of Flags
[151](https://docs.rs#151)//!
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//! A collection of flags is a `FlagSet<T>`. If you are storing the flags in
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//! memory, the raw `FlagSet<T>` type should be used. However, if you want to
[154](https://docs.rs#154)//! receive flags as an input to a function, you should use
[155](https://docs.rs#155)//! `impl Into<FlagSet<T>>`. This allows for very ergonomic APIs:
[156](https://docs.rs#156)//!
[157](https://docs.rs#157)//! ```
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//! use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[159](https://docs.rs#159)//!
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//! flags! {
[161](https://docs.rs#161)//!     enum Flags: u8 {
[162](https://docs.rs#162)//!         Foo,
[163](https://docs.rs#163)//!         Bar,
[164](https://docs.rs#164)//!         Baz,
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//!     }
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//! }
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//!
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//! struct Container(FlagSet<Flags>);
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//!
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//! impl Container {
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//!     fn new(flags: impl Into<FlagSet<Flags>>) -> Container {
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//!         Container(flags.into())
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//!     }
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//! }
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//!
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//! assert_eq!(Container::new(Flags::Foo | Flags::Bar).0.bits(), 0b011);
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//! assert_eq!(Container::new(Flags::Foo).0.bits(), 0b001);
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//! assert_eq!(Container::new(None).0.bits(), 0b000);
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//! ```
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//!
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//! ## Operations
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//!
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//! Operations can be performed on a `FlagSet<F>` or on individual flags:
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//!
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//! | Operator | Assignment Operator | Meaning                |
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//! |----------|---------------------|------------------------|
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//! | \|       | \|=                 | Union                  |
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//! | &        | &=                  | Intersection           |
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//! | ^        | ^=                  | Toggle specified flags |
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//! | -        | -=                  | Difference             |
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//! | %        | %=                  | Symmetric difference   |
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//! | !        |                     | Toggle all flags       |
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//!
[194](https://docs.rs#194)#![cfg_attr(
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    feature = "serde",
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    doc = r#"
[197](https://docs.rs#197)
[198](https://docs.rs#198)## Optional Serde support
[199](https://docs.rs#199)
[200](https://docs.rs#200)[Serde] support can be enabled with the 'serde' feature flag. You can then serialize and
[201](https://docs.rs#201)deserialize `FlagSet<T>` to and from any of the [supported formats]:
[202](https://docs.rs#202)
[203](https://docs.rs#203) ```
[204](https://docs.rs#204) use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[205](https://docs.rs#205)
[206](https://docs.rs#206) flags! {
[207](https://docs.rs#207)     enum Flags: u8 {
[208](https://docs.rs#208)         Foo,
[209](https://docs.rs#209)         Bar,
[210](https://docs.rs#210)     }
[211](https://docs.rs#211) }
[212](https://docs.rs#212)
[213](https://docs.rs#213) let flagset = Flags::Foo | Flags::Bar;
[214](https://docs.rs#214) let json = serde_json::to_string(&flagset).unwrap();
[215](https://docs.rs#215) let flagset: FlagSet<Flags> = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
[216](https://docs.rs#216) assert_eq!(flagset.bits(), 0b011);
[217](https://docs.rs#217) ```
[218](https://docs.rs#218)
[219](https://docs.rs#219)For serialization and deserialization of flags enum itself, you can use the [`serde_repr`] crate
[220](https://docs.rs#220)(or implement `serde::ser::Serialize` and `serde:de::Deserialize` manually), combined with the
[221](https://docs.rs#221)appropriate `repr` attribute:
[222](https://docs.rs#222)
[223](https://docs.rs#223) ```
[224](https://docs.rs#224) use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[225](https://docs.rs#225) use serde_repr::{Serialize_repr, Deserialize_repr};
[226](https://docs.rs#226)
[227](https://docs.rs#227) flags! {
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    #[repr(u8)]
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    #[derive(Deserialize_repr, Serialize_repr)]
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    enum Flags: u8 {
[231](https://docs.rs#231)         Foo,
[232](https://docs.rs#232)         Bar,
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    }
[234](https://docs.rs#234) }
[235](https://docs.rs#235)
[236](https://docs.rs#236) let json = serde_json::to_string(&Flags::Foo).unwrap();
[237](https://docs.rs#237) let flag: Flags = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
[238](https://docs.rs#238) assert_eq!(flag, Flags::Foo);
[239](https://docs.rs#239) ```
[240](https://docs.rs#240)
[241](https://docs.rs#241)[Serde]: https://serde.rs/
[242](https://docs.rs#242)[supported formats]: https://serde.rs/#data-formats
[243](https://docs.rs#243)[`serde_repr`]: https://crates.io/crates/serde_repr

[255](https://docs.rs#255)/// ```

[260](https://docs.rs#260)///         Foo = 0b0001,
[261](https://docs.rs#261)///         Bar = 0b0010,
[262](https://docs.rs#262)///         Baz = 0b0100,
[263](https://docs.rs#263)///         Qux = 0b1010, // Implies Bar
[264](https://docs.rs#264)///     }
[265](https://docs.rs#265)/// }
[266](https://docs.rs#266)///
[267](https://docs.rs#267)/// assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b01101), Err(flagset::InvalidBits)); // Invalid

[334](https://docs.rs#334)impl<F: Flags> Iterator for Iter<F> {
[335](https://docs.rs#335)    type Item = F;
[336](https://docs.rs#336)
[337](https://docs.rs#337)    #[inline]
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
[339](https://docs.rs#339)        while self.1 < F::LIST.len() {
[340](https://docs.rs#340)            let next = F::LIST[self.1];
[341](https://docs.rs#341)            self.1 += 1;
[342](https://docs.rs#342)
[343](https://docs.rs#343)            if self.0.contains(next) {
[344](https://docs.rs#344)                return Some(next);
[345](https://docs.rs#345)            }
[346](https://docs.rs#346)        }
[347](https://docs.rs#347)
[348](https://docs.rs#348)        None
[349](https://docs.rs#349)    }

[408](https://docs.rs#408)impl<F: Flags> From<Option<FlagSet<F>>> for FlagSet<F> {
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    /// Converts from `Option<FlagSet<F>>` to `FlagSet<F>`.
[410](https://docs.rs#410)    ///
[411](https://docs.rs#411)    /// Most notably, this allows for the use of `None` in many places to
[412](https://docs.rs#412)    /// substitute for manually creating an empty `FlagSet<F>`. See below.
[413](https://docs.rs#413)    ///
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    /// ```
[415](https://docs.rs#415)    /// use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[416](https://docs.rs#416)    ///
[417](https://docs.rs#417)    /// flags! {
[418](https://docs.rs#418)    ///     enum Flag: u8 {
[419](https://docs.rs#419)    ///         Foo = 0b001,
[420](https://docs.rs#420)    ///         Bar = 0b010,
[421](https://docs.rs#421)    ///         Baz = 0b100
[422](https://docs.rs#422)    ///     }
[423](https://docs.rs#423)    /// }
[424](https://docs.rs#424)    ///

[721](https://docs.rs#721)impl<F: Flags, R: Into<FlagSet<F>>> Rem<R> for FlagSet<F> {
[722](https://docs.rs#722)    type Output = Self;
[723](https://docs.rs#723)
[724](https://docs.rs#724)    /// Calculates the symmetric difference between two sets.
[725](https://docs.rs#725)    ///
[726](https://docs.rs#726)    /// The symmetric difference between two sets is the set of all flags
[727](https://docs.rs#727)    /// that appear in one set or the other, but not both.
[728](https://docs.rs#728)    ///
[729](https://docs.rs#729)    /// ```
[730](https://docs.rs#730)    /// use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[731](https://docs.rs#731)    ///
[732](https://docs.rs#732)    /// flags! {
[733](https://docs.rs#733)    ///     pub enum Flag: u8 {
[734](https://docs.rs#734)    ///         Foo = 1,
[735](https://docs.rs#735)    ///         Bar = 2,
[736](https://docs.rs#736)    ///         Baz = 4
[737](https://docs.rs#737)    ///     }
[738](https://docs.rs#738)    /// }
[739](https://docs.rs#739)    ///
[740](https://docs.rs#740)    /// let set0 = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
[741](https://docs.rs#741)    /// let set1 = Flag::Baz | Flag::Bar;
[742](https://docs.rs#742)    /// assert_eq!(set0 % set1, Flag::Foo | Flag::Baz);
[743](https://docs.rs#743)    /// ```
[744](https://docs.rs#744)    #[inline]
[745](https://docs.rs#745)    fn rem(self, rhs: R) -> Self {
[746](https://docs.rs#746)        let rhs = rhs.into();
[747](https://docs.rs#747)        (self - rhs) | (rhs - self)
[748](https://docs.rs#748)    }
[749](https://docs.rs#749)}
[750](https://docs.rs#750)
[751](https://docs.rs#751)impl<F: Flags, R: Into<FlagSet<F>>> RemAssign<R> for FlagSet<F> {
[752](https://docs.rs#752)    /// Assigns the symmetric difference between two sets.
[753](https://docs.rs#753)    ///
[754](https://docs.rs#754)    /// The symmetric difference between two sets is the set of all flags
[755](https://docs.rs#755)    /// that appear in one set or the other, but not both.
[756](https://docs.rs#756)    ///
[757](https://docs.rs#757)    /// ```
[758](https://docs.rs#758)    /// use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[759](https://docs.rs#759)    ///
[760](https://docs.rs#760)    /// flags! {
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    ///     pub enum Flag: u8 {
[762](https://docs.rs#762)    ///         Foo = 1,
[763](https://docs.rs#763)    ///         Bar = 2,
[764](https://docs.rs#764)    ///         Baz = 4
[765](https://docs.rs#765)    ///     }
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    /// }
[767](https://docs.rs#767)    ///
[768](https://docs.rs#768)    /// let mut set0 = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
[769](https://docs.rs#769)    /// let set1 = Flag::Baz | Flag::Bar;

[779](https://docs.rs#779)impl<F: Flags, R: Into<FlagSet<F>>> Extend<R> for FlagSet<F> {
[780](https://docs.rs#780)    /// Add values by iterating over some collection.
[781](https://docs.rs#781)    ///
[782](https://docs.rs#782)    /// ```
[783](https://docs.rs#783)    /// use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[784](https://docs.rs#784)    ///
[785](https://docs.rs#785)    /// flags! {
[786](https://docs.rs#786)    ///     pub enum Flag: u8 {
[787](https://docs.rs#787)    ///         Foo = 1,
[788](https://docs.rs#788)    ///         Bar = 2,
[789](https://docs.rs#789)    ///         Baz = 4
[790](https://docs.rs#790)    ///     }
[791](https://docs.rs#791)    /// }
[792](https://docs.rs#792)    ///
[793](https://docs.rs#793)    /// let flag_vec = vec![Flag::Bar, Flag::Baz];
[794](https://docs.rs#794)    /// let mut some_extended_flags = FlagSet::from(Flag::Foo);
[795](https://docs.rs#795)    /// some_extended_flags.extend(flag_vec);
[796](https://docs.rs#796)    /// assert_eq!(some_extended_flags, Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar | Flag::Baz);
[797](https://docs.rs#797)    /// ```
[798](https://docs.rs#798)    fn extend<T>(&mut self, iter: T)
[799](https://docs.rs#799)    where
[800](https://docs.rs#800)        T: IntoIterator<Item = R>,
[801](https://docs.rs#801)    {
[802](https://docs.rs#802)        for item in iter {
[803](https://docs.rs#803)            *self |= item;
[804](https://docs.rs#804)        }
[805](https://docs.rs#805)    }

[809](https://docs.rs#809)    /// Creates a new set from bits; returning `Err(InvalidBits)` on invalid/unknown bits.
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    ///
[811](https://docs.rs#811)    /// ```
[812](https://docs.rs#812)    /// use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[813](https://docs.rs#813)    ///
[814](https://docs.rs#814)    /// flags! {
[815](https://docs.rs#815)    ///     pub enum Flag: u16 {
[816](https://docs.rs#816)    ///         Foo = 0b0001,
[817](https://docs.rs#817)    ///         Bar = 0b0010,
[818](https://docs.rs#818)    ///         Baz = 0b0100,
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    ///         Qux = 0b1010, // Implies Bar
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    ///     }
[821](https://docs.rs#821)    /// }
[822](https://docs.rs#822)    ///
[823](https://docs.rs#823)    /// assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b00101), Ok(Flag::Foo | Flag::Baz));
[824](https://docs.rs#824)    /// assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b01101), Err(flagset::InvalidBits)); // Invalid
[825](https://docs.rs#825)    /// assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b10101), Err(flagset::InvalidBits)); // Unknown
[826](https://docs.rs#826)    /// ```
[827](https://docs.rs#827)    #[inline]
[828](https://docs.rs#828)    pub fn new(bits: F::Type) -> core::result::Result<Self, InvalidBits> {
[829](https://docs.rs#829)        if Self::new_truncated(bits).0 == bits {
[830](https://docs.rs#830)            return Ok(FlagSet(bits));
[831](https://docs.rs#831)        }
[832](https://docs.rs#832)
[833](https://docs.rs#833)        Err(InvalidBits)
[834](https://docs.rs#834)    }
[835](https://docs.rs#835)
[836](https://docs.rs#836)    /// Creates a new set from bits; truncating invalid/unknown bits.
[837](https://docs.rs#837)    ///
[838](https://docs.rs#838)    /// ```
[839](https://docs.rs#839)    /// use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[840](https://docs.rs#840)    ///
[841](https://docs.rs#841)    /// flags! {
[842](https://docs.rs#842)    ///     pub enum Flag: u16 {
[843](https://docs.rs#843)    ///         Foo = 0b0001,
[844](https://docs.rs#844)    ///         Bar = 0b0010,
[845](https://docs.rs#845)    ///         Baz = 0b0100,
[846](https://docs.rs#846)    ///         Qux = 0b1010, // Implies Bar
[847](https://docs.rs#847)    ///     }
[848](https://docs.rs#848)    /// }
[849](https://docs.rs#849)    ///
[850](https://docs.rs#850)    /// let set = FlagSet::new_truncated(0b11101);  // Has invalid and unknown.
[851](https://docs.rs#851)    /// assert_eq!(set, Flag::Foo | Flag::Baz);
[852](https://docs.rs#852)    /// assert_eq!(set.bits(), 0b00101);            // Has neither.
[853](https://docs.rs#853)    /// ```
[854](https://docs.rs#854)    #[inline]
[855](https://docs.rs#855)    pub fn new_truncated(bits: F::Type) -> Self {
[856](https://docs.rs#856)        let mut set = Self::default();
[857](https://docs.rs#857)
[858](https://docs.rs#858)        for flag in FlagSet::<F>(bits) {
[859](https://docs.rs#859)            set |= flag;
[860](https://docs.rs#860)        }
[861](https://docs.rs#861)
[862](https://docs.rs#862)        set
[863](https://docs.rs#863)    }

[865](https://docs.rs#865)    /// Creates a new set from bits; use of invalid/unknown bits is undefined.
[866](https://docs.rs#866)    ///
[867](https://docs.rs#867)    /// ```
[868](https://docs.rs#868)    /// use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
[869](https://docs.rs#869)    ///

[875](https://docs.rs#875)    ///         Qux = 0b1010, // Implies Bar

[877](https://docs.rs#877)    /// }

[890](https://docs.rs#890)        FlagSet(bits)
[891](https://docs.rs#891)    }

[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)/// Define flag value using the `enum` syntax. See below for details.
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)///
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)/// Each enumeration value **MUST** have a specified value.
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)///
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)/// The width of the bitfield **MUST** also be specified by its integer type.
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)///
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)/// It is important to note that the size of the flag enumeration itself is
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)/// unrelated to the size of the corresponding `FlagSet` instance.
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)///
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)/// It is also worth noting that this macro automatically implements a variety
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)/// of standard traits including:

# flags in flagset - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/flagset/latest/target-redirect/flagset/macro.flags.html

```
macro_rules! flags {
    () => { ... };
    ($(#[$m:meta])* $p:vis enum $n:ident: $t:ty { $($(#[$a:meta])* $k:ident),+ $(,)* } $($next:tt)*) => { ... };
    ($(#[$m:meta])* $p:vis enum $n:ident: $t:ty { $($(#[$a:meta])*$k:ident = $v:expr),* $(,)* } $($next:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Define flag value using the `enum` syntax. See below for details.

Each enumeration value **MUST** have a specified value.

The width of the bitfield **MUST** also be specified by its integer type.

It is important to note that the size of the flag enumeration itself is
unrelated to the size of the corresponding `FlagSet` instance.

It is also worth noting that this macro automatically implements a variety of standard traits including:

- Copy
- Clone
- Debug
- PartialEq
- Eq
- From<$enum> for $integer
- Not
- BitAnd
- BitOr
- BitXor
- Sub
- Rem

```
use std::mem::{align_of, size_of};
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum FlagEmpty: u32 {}
    enum Flag8: u8 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
    pub enum Flag16: u16 {
        Foo,
        Bar,
        #[deprecated]
        Baz,
    }
    #[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]
    enum Flag32: u32 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        #[deprecated]
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
    #[repr(u64)]
    enum Flag64: u64 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
    #[repr(u32)]
    enum Flag128: u128 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
assert_eq!(size_of::<Flag8>(), 1);
assert_eq!(size_of::<Flag16>(), 1);
assert_eq!(size_of::<Flag32>(), 1);
assert_eq!(size_of::<Flag64>(), 8);
assert_eq!(size_of::<Flag128>(), 4);
assert_eq!(align_of::<Flag8>(), 1);
assert_eq!(align_of::<Flag16>(), 1);
assert_eq!(align_of::<Flag32>(), 1);
assert_eq!(align_of::<Flag64>(), align_of::<u64>());
assert_eq!(align_of::<Flag128>(), align_of::<u32>());
assert_eq!(size_of::<FlagSet<Flag8>>(), size_of::<u8>());
assert_eq!(size_of::<FlagSet<Flag16>>(), size_of::<u16>());
assert_eq!(size_of::<FlagSet<Flag32>>(), size_of::<u32>());
assert_eq!(size_of::<FlagSet<Flag64>>(), size_of::<u64>());
assert_eq!(size_of::<FlagSet<Flag128>>(), size_of::<u128>());
assert_eq!(align_of::<FlagSet<Flag8>>(), align_of::<u8>());
assert_eq!(align_of::<FlagSet<Flag16>>(), align_of::<u16>());
assert_eq!(align_of::<FlagSet<Flag32>>(), align_of::<u32>());
assert_eq!(align_of::<FlagSet<Flag64>>(), align_of::<u64>());
assert_eq!(align_of::<FlagSet<Flag128>>(), align_of::<u128>());
```

use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    pub enum Flag: u16 {
        Foo = 0b0001,
        Bar = 0b0010,
        Baz = 0b0100,
        Qux = 0b1010, // Implies Bar
    }
}
assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b00101), Ok(Flag::Foo | Flag::Baz));
assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b01101), Err(flagset::InvalidBits)); // Invalid
assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b10101), Err(flagset::InvalidBits)); // Unknown
```

#### pub const unsafe fn [new_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.new_unchecked)(bits: F::Type) -> Self

Creates a new set from bits; use of invalid/unknown bits is undefined.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    pub enum Flag: u16 {
        Foo = 0b0001,
        Bar = 0b0010,
        Baz = 0b0100,
        Qux = 0b1010, // Implies Bar
    }
}
// Unknown and invalid bits are retained. Behavior is undefined.
const set: FlagSet<Flag> = unsafe { FlagSet::<Flag>::new_unchecked(0b11101) };
assert_eq!(set.bits(), 0b11101);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

This constructor doesn’t check that the bits are valid. If you pass undefined flags, undefined behavior may result.

Creates a new, empty FlagSet.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}

assert!(set.is_empty());
assert!(!set.is_full());
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Foo));
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Bar));
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Baz));
```
Creates a new FlagSet containing all possible flags.

        Baz = 4

Clears the current set and returns an iterator of all removed flags.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

Calculates the intersection of the current set and the specified flags.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    #[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]
    pub enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
let set0 = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
let set1 = Flag::Baz | Flag::Bar;
assert_eq!(set0 & set1, Flag::Bar);
assert_eq!(set0 & Flag::Foo, Flag::Foo);
assert_eq!(set1 & Flag::Baz, Flag::Baz);
```

Assigns the intersection of the current set and the specified flags.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u64 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
let mut set0 = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
let mut set1 = Flag::Baz | Flag::Bar;
set0 &= set1;
assert_eq!(set0, Flag::Bar);
set1 &= Flag::Baz;
assert_eq!(set0, Flag::Bar);
```
Calculates the union of the current set with the specified flags.

    pub enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }

#### fn [bitor_assign](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/bit/trait.BitOrAssign.html#tymethod.bitor_assign)(&mut self, rhs: R)

Assigns the union of the current set with the specified flags.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u64 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }

Calculates the current set with the specified flags toggled.

This is commonly known as toggling the presence

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u32 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
let set0 = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
let set1 = Flag::Baz | Flag::Bar;
assert_eq!(set0 ^ set1, Flag::Foo | Flag::Baz);
assert_eq!(set0 ^ Flag::Foo, Flag::Bar);
```

Creates a new, empty FlagSet.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
let set = FlagSet::<Flag>::default();
assert!(set.is_empty());
assert!(!set.is_full());
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Foo));
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Bar));
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Baz));
```
Add values by iterating over some collection.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    pub enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 1,
        Bar = 2,
        Baz = 4
    }
}
let flag_vec = vec![Flag::Bar, Flag::Baz];
let mut some_extended_flags = FlagSet::from(Flag::Foo);
some_extended_flags.extend(flag_vec);
assert_eq!(some_extended_flags, Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar | Flag::Baz);
```
Converts from `Option<FlagSet<F>>` to `FlagSet<F>`.

Most notably, this allows for the use of `None` in many places to
substitute for manually creating an empty `FlagSet<F>`. See below.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
fn convert(v: impl Into<FlagSet<Flag>>) -> u8 {
    v.into().bits()
}
assert_eq!(convert(Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar), 0b011);
assert_eq!(convert(Flag::Foo), 0b001);
assert_eq!(convert(None), 0b000);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/flagset/lib.rs.html#352-381)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-IntoIterator-for-FlagSet%3CF%3E)

### impl<F: Flags> [IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html) for [FlagSet](https://docs.rs/struct.FlagSet.html)<F>

Iterate over the flags in the set.

**NOTE**: The order in which the flags are iterated is undefined.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 0b001,
        Bar = 0b010,
        Baz = 0b100
    }
}
let set = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
let mut iter = set.into_iter();
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(Flag::Foo));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(Flag::Bar));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), None);
```
Calculates the complement of the current set.

In common parlance, this returns the set of all possible flags that are not in the current set.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    #[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]
    enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 1 << 0,
        Bar = 1 << 1,
        Baz = 1 << 2
    }
}
let set = !FlagSet::from(Flag::Foo);
assert!(!set.is_empty());
assert!(!set.is_full());
assert!(!set.contains(Flag::Foo));
assert!(set.contains(Flag::Bar));
assert!(set.contains(Flag::Baz));
```
Calculates the symmetric difference between two sets.

The symmetric difference between two sets is the set of all flags that appear in one set or the other, but not both.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    pub enum Flag: u8 {
        Foo = 1,
        Bar = 2,
        Baz = 4
    }
}
let set0 = Flag::Foo | Flag::Bar;
let set1 = Flag::Baz | Flag::Bar;
assert_eq!(set0 % set1, Flag::Foo | Flag::Baz);
```

# InvalidBits in flagset - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/flagset/latest/target-redirect/flagset/struct.InvalidBits.html

`pub struct InvalidBits;`## Expand description

Error type returned when creating a new flagset from bits is invalid or undefined.

```
use flagset::{FlagSet, flags};
flags! {
    pub enum Flag: u16 {
        Foo = 0b0001,
        Bar = 0b0010,
        Baz = 0b0100,
        Qux = 0b1010, // Implies Bar
    }
}
assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b01101), Err(flagset::InvalidBits)); // Invalid
assert_eq!(FlagSet::<Flag>::new(0b10101), Err(flagset::InvalidBits)); // Unknown
```

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
- [clap-verbosity-flag](https://crates.io/crates/clap-verbosity-flag)
- [clap-cargo](https://crates.io/crates/clap-cargo)
- [colorchoice-clap](https://crates.io/crates/colorchoice-clap)

Testing

- `trycmd`
- `snapbox`
- `assert_cmd`- `assert_fs`
